Marcus (cust)-AcmeAI: Hey team, we've been seeing a ton of 502s and 200ms -> 1.2s latency spikes since 06:00 UTC. Our app is in eu-west-1 and we have Dedicated capacity there, but traffic seems to be landing in hosted US pools. Billing spiked too. Can someone help?

Alice (support): Sorry you're hitting this Marcus — curating the escalation. Can you confirm request headers (region header) and whether you're using the customer region pinning config?

Marcus (cust)-AcmeAI: We set region=eu-west-1 in the config and pin=true in the tenant settings. Our clients send X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1. Example curl we use:

curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk.acme..." -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-xyz","input":"hi"}'

Alice (support): Got it. Jia, tagging you — symptoms: unexpected fallback to hosted, cross-region latency, auth 401 on some requests, and billing surge.

Jia (eng-oncall): Investigating. Marcus, can you paste one raw request ID (x-request-id) from a failing call? Also, were any credentials rotated recently?

Marcus (cust)-AcmeAI: x-request-id: req_0b9f3a9c. No key rotations on our side.

deploy-bot: [deploy] router-service v3.14.2 promoted at 05:42 UTC by tom.deploy

Tom (routing-eng): Looking at router logs for req_0b9f3a9c — I see tenant=acme, desired_region=eu-west-1, but routing decision went to pool=hosted-us-east-1. The router emitted fallback_reason=NO_ACTIVE_DEDICATED_IN_REGION. However the dedicated pool for acme in eu-west-1 shows active capacity. Hmm.

Jia (eng-oncall): Can you paste the affinity key hash being computed? I suspect the affinity cache used an old mapping.

Tom (routing-eng): From logs: affinity_key=tenant:acme:region:eu-west-1 -> cache_miss=false -> bound_pool=hosted-us-east-1. That "bound_pool" looks wrong — it should be dedicated-eu-west-1. The cache value appears stale (value: hosted-us-east-1).

Alice (support): Marcus — any recent config changes to TTL or region rename?

Marcus (cust)-AcmeAI: No changes from our side. We did update the dedicated reservation yesterday but that was via sales portal.

Nina (billing): Noting billing impact. If traffic went to hosted-us-east-1, usage will be at on-demand rates. We'll flag for potential credit pending root cause.

Tom (routing-eng): Repro attempt: I forced a request with X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1 and X-Tenant: acme, router returned hosted fallback for ~15% of requests during 05:30-06:10 UTC window. Setting header X-Trace: trace123 — trace: https://traces.internal/trace123 (private).

Sara (platform PM): Is this related to the router cache refresh? We rolled a caching change in v3.14.2 earlier today per the deploy-bot note.

Tom (routing-eng): Possible. The change adjusts cache key normalization to remove tenant metadata that included region aliasing. Looks like some tenants still had old alias mapping (eu-west vs eu-west-1) and cache entries with alias were not invalidated properly. When cache returned alias-mapped pool, fallback logic treated it as incompatible and forwarded to hosted.

Jia (eng-oncall): That explains cross-region fallthrough and 401s: some hosted pools require regional token binding; an auth middleware checks token-region against pool-region and rejects mismatched tokens. Marcus, can you confirm whether your tokens include a region claim?

Marcus (cust)-AcmeAI: Our tokens are region-bound (claim "r":"eu-west-1"). We saw some 401s that correlate with requests routed to us-east pools.

Alice (support): Action items so far: (1) Tom to invalidate affinity cache for acme; (2) Jia to roll hotfix to ensure cache-key normalization back-compat; (3) Nina to prepare rebate estimate; (4) Sara to coordinate postmortem.

Tom (routing-eng): Invalidation executed at 06:12 UTC for tenant=acme. I pushed a targeted cache purge and confirmed subsequent requests route to dedicated-eu-west-1.

Marcus (cust)-AcmeAI: After purge latency dropped back to ~80ms and 200s returned. Thanks. We still saw a billing uptick for the 40m window.

Nina (billing): Please open a support billing ticket referencing thread req_0b9f3a9c + timestamp window 05:30-06:10 UTC. I'll fast-track review and propose a partial credit.

Jia (eng-oncall): I'll backport a fix to router v3.14.x to ensure alias invalidation on config change. Patch includes additional cache versioning metadata and safe fallback prevention. Plan: v3.14.3 hotfix in 2 hours.

Sara (platform PM): Also adding safety net: disable cross-region automatic fallback for tenants with region-bound auth tokens until we have confidence. That reduces availability risk but avoids auth failures. Going to propose in change-review.

Tom (routing-eng): Quick repro steps I used for validation for ops docs:
1) curl with bad alias header: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk.acme..." -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west" -H "X-Tenant: acme" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -v
```
2) Observe router log: affinity_key contains alias 'eu-west' and returns hosted pool mapping.
3) Purge cache: POST /internal/cache/purge tenant=acme
4) Retry with canonical header: X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1 -> should land in dedicated pool.

Alice (support): Marcus — apologies for the disruption. We'll follow up with a ticket for billing adjustment and a summary postmortem when Sara has it. Anything else on your end?

Marcus (cust)-AcmeAI: Appreciate the fast triage. Please confirm when hotfix is in prod so we can relax our retry/backoff aggressions.

Jia (eng-oncall): Hotfix scheduled 08:30 UTC, monitoring for 1hr. We'll post status here once live.

deploy-bot: [deploy] router-service v3.14.3 scheduled at 08:30 UTC by jia.ops

Tom (routing-eng): Follow-up: created internal doc /runbooks/routing/affinity-alias-invalidation.md with the purge steps and a checklist to run after reservation changes.

Nina (billing): Billing ticket created (#BILL-4987). Will update Marcus by EOD.

Sara (platform PM): Postmortem scheduled for tomorrow 15:00 UTC. I'll include impact metrics (latency histogram, percent routed to hosted, estimated cost delta).

Marcus (cust)-AcmeAI: Thanks all — marking resolved for now.

Alice (support): Closing loop: root cause = cache entries with region alias (eu-west) not invalidated after reservation update -> stale bound_pool -> fallback to hosted-US causing cross-region latency + auth 401s for region-bound tokens -> billing spike. Mitigations: cache purge, hotfix for normalization + invalidation, temporary disable cross-region fallback for region-bound tenants, billing review. :white_check_mark:
